# reselling_rootserver (Resource)

A rootserver (KVM virtual machine). Creation waits until the installation finished. `cores`, `ram`, `disk` and `bandwidth_tier_id` are changed in place through a resize; the disk can only grow, a smaller `disk` replaces the server. `hostname`, `labels`, `notes`, `ssh_key_ids`, `admin_password` and the IP counts are changed in place.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "reselling_locations" "fra" {
  name = "Frankfurt"
}

data "reselling_os_versions" "debian" {
  name    = "debian"
  version = "12"
}

resource "reselling_rootserver" "web" {
  cluster_id    = data.reselling_locations.fra.locations[0].clusters[0].id
  os_version_id = data.reselling_os_versions.debian.versions[0].id
  hostname      = "web01.example.com"
  cores         = 2
  ram           = 4096 # MB
  disk          = 40   # GB
  ipv4_count    = 1
  ipv6_count    = 1
  ssh_key_ids   = [reselling_ssh_key.admin.id]
  labels        = ["web"]

  # Write-only (Terraform 1.11+): only its SHA-256 is kept in the state.
  user_data = <<-EOT
    #cloud-config
    packages: [nginx]
  EOT

  # Delete this volume together with the server; volumes not listed are kept.
  volume_on_delete {
    volume_id = reselling_rootserver_volume.data.id
    action    = "delete"
  }

  timeouts {
    create = "45m"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cluster_id` (String) Hardware cluster the server runs on (see data source `reselling_locations`). Changing it replaces the server.
- `cores` (Number) CPU cores. Changed in place (resize).
- `disk` (Number) System disk in GB (at least 10). Grows in place; a smaller value replaces the server.
- `hostname` (String) Hostname or FQDN. Changed in place.
- `ram` (Number) Memory in MB (at least 512). Changed in place (resize).

### Optional

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `admin_password` (String, Sensitive) Root/Administrator password. Generated when not set. A changed value resets the password in place. Read back only when the API key holds `rootservers:update`.
- `bandwidth_tier_id` (String) Bandwidth tier of the cluster (see `reselling_locations`). Changed in place (resize).
- `delete_protection` (Boolean) Protect the server from deletion. While it is on, `terraform destroy` fails for this server.
- `image_id` (String) Custom image to install instead of an operating system (see `reselling_rootserver_image`). Changing it replaces the server.
- `ipv4_count` (Number) Number of IPv4 addresses (0 for an IPv6-only Linux server). Default 1. More addresses are ordered in place, fewer remove the newest secondary addresses.
- `ipv6_count` (Number) Number of IPv6 /64 subnets. Default 1. Changed in place.
- `labels` (List of String) Up to 10 labels (1-32 characters). Firewall groups and load balancer targets can select servers by label.
- `notes` (String) Free-text note.
- `os_version_id` (String) Operating system version to install (see data source `reselling_os_versions`). Exactly one of `os_version_id` and `image_id` is required. Changing it replaces the server.
- `ssh_key_ids` (Set of String) Ids of stored SSH keys (`reselling_ssh_key`). Keys are added to and removed from the running server in place.
- `startup_script_id` (String) Startup script that runs on installation. Changing it replaces the server.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))
- `user_data` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) cloud-init user data (`#cloud-config` or a script starting with `#!`, Linux only, max. 32768 bytes) that runs on the first boot. Write-only: the content is never stored in the state, only its SHA-256 in `user_data_sha256`. A changed content replaces the server. Requires Terraform 1.11 or later.
- `volume_on_delete` (Block List) What happens to an attached volume when the server is deleted. Volumes not listed are kept (detached, they stay in the account and keep being billed). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--volume_on_delete))

### Read-Only

- `admin_user` (String)
- `has_user_data` (Boolean) Whether the server has user data stored.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `ipv4_addresses` (List of String) All IPv4 addresses.
- `ipv6_subnets` (List of String) All IPv6 subnets.
- `location_id` (String) Location of the cluster.
- `primary_ip` (String) Primary IPv4 address.
- `status` (String) Status, for example `running` or `stopped`.
- `user_data_sha256` (String) SHA-256 of the user data that was sent on creation.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).


<a id="nestedblock--volume_on_delete"></a>
### Nested Schema for `volume_on_delete`

Required:

- `action` (String) `keep` or `delete`.
- `volume_id` (String)

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import reselling_rootserver.web <server_id>
```
